newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices up, brokers see further rise.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices up, brokers see further rise.

text.p: Egyptian share prices firmed on Tuesday and brokers forecast the market would keep rising.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index edged 0.30 points up to 234.40. Volume was a high 109.96 million pounds ($32.34 million) with the registration of new privatisation Arab Cotton Ginning accounting for just 29 percent.

Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose on strong demand last week, again led the market upwards. The shares, the bourse's most active, ended 7.75 pounds higher at 157.75 on rumours of a GDR offering.
Reports of a GDR in Suez Cement continued to push prices upwards and shares ended 2.15 pounds higher at 50.00.
Helwan Portland Cement was a close second, gaining 3.90 to 49.90 while Egyptian Portland Tora Cement also rose 1.00 to 63.60.
Rumours that Egypt's state owned National Bank of Egypt may sell its stake in joint venture bank Nationale Societe Generale boosted shares 9.00 pounds to 445.00.
Brokers said they thought French investors and a foreign fund were snapping up any quantities of the bank's shares.
"The bourse has reached the stage where you cannot buy a share, it's in a very strong uptrend," said Adel el-Dakroury, a broker at Triple A Securities.
But a trader said foreign fund managers visiting the headquarters of several listed companies, including blue-chip cement and milling firms, were behind the rally.
"The moment the foreigners walked out of the company, their share prices shot up," he said. "Guess everyone thought they were coming to buy when they were only paying courtesy calls."
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 351.73 points from Monday's 352.43 and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose marginally to 160.29 points from 160.28.
